key_insight: Bayesian Dialectical Argumentation turns a multi-LLM council’s debate trace into per-agent reliability estimates, producing calibrated probabilities and resilience to persistently unreliable or adversarial models.
engineering_relevance: It offers a zero-extra-call aggregation layer for deployed LLM councils where both confidence calibration and robustness to bad actors matter.
method: Treat typed debate moves (propose, challenge, concede) as observations in a classical annotator model.
Infer per-agent reliabilities with Bayesian updates from the deliberation trace.
Weight or invert agent contributions to produce posterior probabilities over candidate answers.
evidence_signal: Across binary and multi-class benchmarks, the method is reported to achieve the best calibration among zero-cost council aggregation methods and stronger robustness under persistent adversarial coalitions, while remaining competitive in clean settings.
watch_item: Performance depends on informative deliberation traces; if agent actions are sparse, noisy, or strategically opaque, reliability inference may be less dependable.
paper_title: Counting Moves, Weighing Voices: Bayesian Dialectical Argumentation for Calibrated Multi-LLM Councils under Persistent Adversaries
